newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision starts privatisation process.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision starts privatisation process.

text.p: Spanish state telecommunications firm Retevision is taking a first step towards privatisation this week by selecting the bank which will manage the sale process.
By the end of the week Retevision may announce which investment bank it has chosen to pick a "core" group of investors for the initial public offering, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
A total of 10 European and U.S. investment banks are competing for the contract.

The privatisation of Retevision aims to turn it into Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica and is due to be completed by 2000. Currently, the company focuses almost exclusively on transmitting audiovisual signals.
The state will initially sell between 51 and 60 percent of capital to a small nucleus of shareholders. This process may start in October, the company said.
In a second tranche, it will sell another 20 percent although it was not clear whether this would be to small shareholders or the existing core investors.
The start of the privatisation process depends on parliamentary approval, which could delay it until early next year.
Among those likely to compete for a stake is a consortium formed by Endesa, Banco Central Hispano and Banco Santander.

Financial daily Expansion reported multinational group Global One -- formed by France Telecom, Deutsche Telecom and Sprint -- as well as Britain's British Telecom and Cable & Wireless had shown interest.
